scenes.title: A Story Jesus Told
beats: Jesus was always making friends with people that nobody else liked. Some people grumbled about it. “Why does He eat with people like that?”
So Jesus told them a story.

layers.prompt: One single continuous scene that fills the whole picture from edge to edge, with no blank paper, no book page, no fold and no seam: On a sunny hillside dotted with olive trees: Jesus sits on a big rock, right of center, telling a story with His hand raised, while a mixed group of people sit on the grass around Him listening closely, children leaning in, and two stern, grumbling religious teachers in tall hats and fancy robes stand off to one side with their arms crossed

scenes.title: One Hundred Sheep
beats: “Once there was a shepherd who had one hundred sheep,” Jesus said. “He loved every single one of them.”
Every evening, the shepherd counted his sheep as they went into the pen. “Ninety-seven, ninety-eight, ninety-nine…” Wait! One little lamb was missing!

layers.prompt: One single continuous scene that fills the whole picture from edge to edge, with no blank paper, no book page, no fold and no seam: In the golden evening light on rolling green hills: the shepherd stands at the gate of a round stone sheep pen, right of center, counting a long line of fluffy white sheep as they trot in, his staff raised and a worried look on his face as he notices one is missing; the pen is full of sheep

scenes.title: Looking Everywhere
beats: The shepherd left the ninety-nine sheep safe in the pen, and off he went to look for the one that was lost.
He looked over the hills and down in the valleys. He looked behind rocks and through prickly bushes. It was getting dark, but he kept on calling, “Little lamb! Where are you?”

layers.prompt: One single continuous scene that fills the whole picture from edge to edge, with no blank paper, no book page, no fold and no seam: Rocky hills at dusk under a deep blue sky with the first stars: the shepherd climbs a steep, rocky path, right of center, holding up a glowing clay oil lamp and calling out with his hand cupped to his mouth, his staff in his other hand, searching among the boulders and thorny bushes

scenes.title: Found!
beats: Then he heard it: a tiny little “Baa!” There was the lamb, stuck in a thorny bush, cold and scared.
The shepherd gently lifted the little lamb out and put it up on his shoulders. He wasn’t cross at all. He was so happy! And he carried it all the way home.

layers.prompt: One single continuous moonlit scene that fills the whole picture from edge to edge, with no panels, no blank paper, no book page, no fold and no seam: a rocky hillside at night under a starry sky with a big moon; a small, frightened fluffy white lamb is stuck in a tangled thorny bush on a little ledge a bit left of center, looking up hopefully, while on the right the shepherd comes around the boulders toward it, holding up his warm glowing lamp; boulders, grass tufts and night sky continue all the way to the left and right edges

layers.edit: The shepherd now carries the little lamb safely across his shoulders, holding its legs gently, smiling with joy, and the lamb snuggles its face against his head; the thorny bush is behind them, and soft golden light glows around them.

scenes.title: Rejoice With Me!
beats: When he got home, the shepherd called all his friends and neighbors. “Come and celebrate with me! I found my lost sheep!”
Then Jesus said, “That is how God feels. All of heaven has a party whenever one lost person comes home to God.”
You are like that little lamb. God loves you so much, He will always come looking for you.

layers.prompt: One single continuous scene that fills the whole picture from edge to edge, with no blank paper, no book page, no fold and no seam: In a lantern-lit village courtyard in the evening: the shepherd dances happily with the little lamb still on his shoulders, right of center, while friends and neighbors laugh, clap, play a tambourine and a little flute, and children dance around them, with strings of lanterns, food on a table and a starry sky above

questions: Why didn’t the shepherd just stay home with his ninety-nine other sheep?
How do you think the little lamb felt when the shepherd found it?
Jesus said God is like that shepherd. How does it feel to know God will always come looking for you?

verse.text: Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost sheep!
